### Step 1 — Scene
A breakfast tray with three fried eggs, brown toast pieces, a yogurt pot, milky tea or coffee, a small bottle of milk, and water. I’m treating the items grouped on the tray as one meal.

### Step 2 — Vessels
- **Egg plate:** approximately 20 cm diameter; area = 3.14 × 10² = **314 cm²**.
- **Toast plate:** approximately 20 cm diameter; area = **314 cm²**.
- For the yogurt and drinks, I use approximate internal food/liquid diameters and filled heights.

### Steps 3–7 — Items, coverage, volume, weight, and energy
Coverage percentages refer to each item’s own vessel. Liquid heights are approximate average filled depths, allowing for vessel shape.

| Item | Vessel area covered | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Three fried eggs | 65% of egg plate | 204 cm² × 0.8 cm = 163 ml | 0.95 | 155 g | 196 | 304 kcal |
| Brown toast pieces | 42% of toast plate | 132 cm² × 1.5 cm = 198 ml | 0.30 | 60 g | 260 | 156 kcal |
| Fruit yogurt, contents only | 100% of ~6 cm internal diameter | 28.3 cm² × 5.3 cm = 150 ml | 1.0 | 150 g | 100 | 150 kcal |
| Milk in bottle | 100% of ~6.5 cm internal diameter | 33.2 cm² × 5.9 cm = 196 ml | 1.03 | 200 g | 50 | 100 kcal |
| Milky tea or coffee | 100% of ~8 cm internal diameter | 50.2 cm² × 4.4 cm = 221 ml | 1.0 | 220 g | 10 | 22 kcal |
| Water | 100% of ~6.5 cm internal diameter | 33.2 cm² × 5.4 cm = 179 ml | 1.0 | 180 g | 0 | 0 kcal |

The egg plate is approximately **65% covered**, and the toast plate approximately **42% covered**. No separate pool of oil or sauce is clearly visible; the fried-egg energy estimate includes cooking fat.

### Step 8 — Sanity check
About **155 g for three eggs** and **60 g of toast** are plausible for the visible portions. Estimated food weight is **365 g**, or **965 g including all drinks and water**. Total energy is approximately **730 kcal**. The largest uncertainties are the yogurt’s fill level and the milk content of the hot drink.
